text: Module two. How somebody becomes a caretaker, and what they see of it afterwards.
Registering is a form: name, the number they will sign in with, and a zone.
Then a question worth slowing down for. Enrol them now, and you are recorded as the approver. Or file them for review, and nobody is.
A national ID scan goes to a restricted bucket and is never displayed — not on the form, not in the directory, not through the API. The record says only that one is on file.
Whoever was filed for review waits here. Each card is one person, with when they registered — some have been waiting months.
Approving records who decided. That is the whole reason this queue exists rather than everyone being enrolled on sight.
And approving is not the end of it. A caretaker with no section has an app listing no trees, and the evening sweep then holds their pay for not logging work nobody assigned.
The directory is everybody, whatever their status — searchable by name or by the number they sign in with.
On the phone, the same decision reads as one line: your zone, and whether you are active.
Under it, what the month adds up to. Trees in your care, logs recorded, days worked.
One screen was deliberately left out. The certification ladder is mock data — a level nobody can reach and badges nobody can earn — so documenting it would describe a feature that does not exist.
Four pages, two surfaces, one person's path into the programme.
